newsitem.title: USA: PP&L sees Susquehanna nuke restart next wk.
newsitem.headline: PP&L sees Susquehanna nuke restart next wk.

text.p: Restart of the 1,090 megawatt (MW) Susquehanna 1 nuclear unit was postponed to next week because work needed to be performed on its residual heat removal system, Pennsylvania Power and Light Co (PP&L) said Friday.
"It's probably not going to happen until the very end of the weekend or early Monday at the earliest," a PP&L spokeswoman said.
Susquehanna 1, in Berwick, Pa., was taken off line February 25 in anticipation of a loss of vacuum in the unit's main condenser. Restart of the unit was interrupted early Tuesday.
The adjoining unit 2, at 1,094 MW, is ramping down for its refueling outage, which is set to begin March 15.
Th two Susquehanna units are jointly owned by PP&L and Allegheny Electric Cooperative Inc.
The Susquehanna facility accounts for 30 percent of PP&L's power deliveries and 20 percent of its installed generation capacity.
